issues.reason: The calibration line protects this: locative deixis is genuinely uncovered (the reviewer's own gap), and (Location sk_counterpunch_1 there) is true of the sentence and well-typed — Location is the licensed event-side oblique on an event-noun eventuality, and a bare untyped constant is exactly how the instruction set already handles deictic 'yesterday' / 'now' (never a witness, never a Member atom); dropping 'out' loses surface detail but makes nothing false.

gaps_confirmed: deictic locative adverbs ('out there', 'here') — deictic constants are defined for time only, and Location / preposition-named obliques expect an NP object

an occupational/role title as an honorific ('Manager Lloyd McClendon') — the title rule covers kinship and courtesy titles only, leaving it unsettled whether 'Manager' stays in the Name string or becomes a typing atom
new_gaps: a direct quotation reported with a speech verb ("P," X said) has no construction of its own — the non-factive attitude route is the only landing place, and nothing carries the quotative/verbatim status or the inverted 'X said' order
a multi-word locative deictic ('out there') has no way to keep the particle: neither a compound-symbol route (compounding is defined for kinds and verbs) nor a preposition-named oblique fits
notes: The say attitude, the sealed content, the existential witness for 'some counterpunching' and the tense placed directly on the event-noun witness are all correct. Keeping 'Manager' inside the Name string follows the Dr Okoro pattern as closely as the title rule allows.
